# Tokenization — Remaining Work Plan

**Purpose:** What's left to fully tokenize the dashboard, in priority order. For current counts, see the Measurement Log in `Token_Migration_Log.md` — figures are not repeated here as static text, since this plan's phases don't change even when the underlying numbers do.

**Source data:** `Hardcoded_Colour_Audit.csv`, regenerated by `python3 tools/colour_audit.py` from the project root (see `Token_Migration_Log.md` for the method). The script is committed — the earlier version lived outside version control, which is why the CSV went missing at migration and had to be regenerated.

---

## Colour — remaining phases

**Phase 1 — Free wins.** Some hardcoded colours already exactly match a defined token (see `matches_existing_token` column in the audit CSV — this column is populated fresh each time the CSV is regenerated, so check it directly rather than a remembered count). Mechanical find-and-replace, zero design decisions.

**Phase 2 — Consolidate near-duplicate clusters.** The unmatched colours in the audit CSV include visually-close clusters (pale tints, greys, near-identical greens/reds) likely re-picked by hand each time rather than reused. Check actual CSS role (background vs. border vs. text) before merging any cluster — near-identical hex values have turned out to be genuinely different states before, not duplicates.

**`rgba()` is in scope for Phase 2 and was previously invisible.** Audit script v1 matched hex only, so a set of `rgba()` occurrences never appeared in the CSV or the counts at all — see the v1-to-v2 reconciliation in `Token_Migration_Log.md`. These are disproportionately pale tints and shadow washes, which is exactly the Phase 2 cluster shape. The audit script prints repeat-use values directly; work that list rather than eyeballing the CSV.

**Phase 3 — Name and token the true remainder.** Whatever's left after Phases 1–2 gets a proper new token following the existing `--color-*` naming convention.

## Spacing

Scale exists (`--space-0`–`--space-7`), applied only to recently-built components. Same find-and-replace/consolidate approach as colour — audit first (see Measurement Log), don't guess which pixel values are meant to be equivalent.

## Text

Scale exists (`--text-xs/sm/base/md/lg`), applied only to recently-built components.

## Approach

Progressive, not a rewrite: token a component fully whenever it's touched for any other reason. No phase here requires a dedicated work session on its own — Phase 1 (colour) is the only one safe to batch-execute independently, since it's pure substitution against values already agreed.

**Before starting any phase:** re-run the audit and check the Measurement Log's latest row for each relevant metric. Don't rely on a remembered number from a previous conversation or an earlier version of this plan.
